summary: Officers pursued an ATV southbound through an east alley off Martin Luther King Jr. Boulevard toward Brown Street; a search of the neighborhood and the tracks afterward did not turn up the rider.
Officers were sent to the 1,400 block of 2nd Street for a disturbance where a teenager was reported to have thrown a chair at the person who called.

Fire crews worked a vegetation fire of about three and a half acres off Washington Street, a couple of streets south of East California Avenue, reporting good progress and expecting to tie in a patrol line within about ten minutes; crews also staffed a second fire nearby.

Officers were sent to the 1,600 block of Rench Road for a teenager reported to be holding a knife in the living room of a home, in the company of his parents; it was not known whether he had brandished it or made threats.
Officers were sent north of Derby Acres for a silver pickup with front-end collision damage that had hit an unknown vehicle and left; a passing motorist reported it.
A gray SUV struck multiple vehicles on the 4,900 block of Hartlepool Avenue.
Medics were requested for a one-year-old who fell at an apartment and was reported unresponsive.
Officers were working a possible hit and run involving a vehicle and a pedestrian, and the person struck was taken to a hospital.

Deputies were sent to the 8,200 block of East Brundage Lane after a call with no voice contact and a juvenile heard crying in the background; the caller later said the noise was coming from an apartment at the front.
Officers were asked to find a man who had taken a large amount of unknown medication, last associated with the 2,800 block of Buddy Drive.
Fire crews were sent to a fire along westbound Highway 58 just west of the Mount Vernon Avenue exit, where a second ambulance was requested and a traffic break was set up.
Officers were sent to the 1,700 block of Glenwood Drive after a woman reported that her caregiver had assaulted her.

Officers chased a man who ran from a suspicious person call at a storage yard on the 4,000 block of Chester Avenue, reaching for his waistband as he ran; he climbed onto a roof on the 3,300 block of Anderson Street and, with Air 1 overhead and a K-9 in place, came down and was arrested, with charges for resisting added.
Fire crews and medics were sent to the 3,000 block of Pioneer Drive for a traumatic injury.
Officers chased a man who ran eastbound on Sky Ranch; a driver and a passenger were taken into custody at a residence on Suncrest Drive, with one person still outstanding.

Officers were sent to a market on the 3,400 block of Pioneer Drive near Sterling after a caller reported two to three people removing boxes of merchandise through an open gate, one holding an object the caller believed was a firearm.

Deputies were sent to the 11,500 block of Old River Road for a person reported to be brandishing a knife; a group was in a gold pickup, one of them holding the knife, and one person reported an assault.
Firefighters and sheriff's deputies searched a remote area north of Kramer along Highway 395 after a caller reported a diabetic emergency; crews found the patient and started an ambulance.
Fire crews and police were sent to the 2,200 block of Sosa Drive for an intentional overdose.
Fire crews were sent to an outside fire near the 8,000 block of Panama Road.
Officers were told of a break-in to a garage and to a vehicle at a home; there was no suspect information.
Officers made contact with a homeowner reported to be possibly disoriented, who agreed to be checked by medics.
Medics were sent to the 1,100 block of Poulsen Way for a person having difficulty breathing.
Fire crews were sent to a residential fire alarm at the 1,400 block of Royal Way; there were no exposures or threats in the area.
Medics were sent to a bus stop at East Roberts Lane and North Chester Avenue for an unknown medical aid after a 911 hang-up.
Officers were sent to a domestic call where a woman told dispatchers she was being abused by her child's father and then disconnected, with an infant heard crying in the background.
A traffic collision was reported near Airport Drive.

Officers were sent to the 400 block of Quantico Avenue where a person went to a residence over a stolen cell phone, broke a window and was in a shouting match with two men who would not let her leave.
Deputies were sent to a disturbance where a man was reported to have pinned his mother against a wall during an argument with a juvenile; a court order was already in place.
Medics were sent to the 10,500 block of Meacham Road for a first-time seizure.
Officers cleared a traffic hazard on Stockdale Highway just west of River Run.
Person suffers cardiac arrest near Belmont Avenue.
Traumatic injury reported on Meyer Road with two facilities present.
Multiple gunshots heard near El Encanto Court.
Two subjects found unconscious in vehicle at Fast Trip.
Two-vehicle crash on westbound 58 near Cottonwood.
Officers attempt contact with reporting party.
